verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. No declaration was found that states the scalar identity itself; what Lean has is the matrix whose quadratic form it is, written in a form that already performs the display's cancellation. Coordinates in `Space = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` are radial, angular, axial (file header, MovingFrameODE.lean:14), `tail w = !₂[w 1, w 2] = w_tan` and `pack r w = !₂[r, w 0, w 1]`, so `baseAction F g t` has radial component -2F t_θ and tangential component t_r • ((2F) e_θ + g): this is exactly the matrix K of the paper's (7.6), rows (0,-2F,0), (2F+RF_R,0,0), (G_R,0,0), once g = (R F_R, G_R) (paper p. 74: "set F = V/R and g = (RF_R, G_R)"), which is `shearVector`. Sign convention agrees: `baseAction` is passed as the argument `Kt` of `TangentProjection.projectedRhs` (TangentProjection.lean:30), matching t' + K t + ... = -f in (7.5). The rewriting is one step: ⟪t, baseAction F g t⟫ = t_r(-2F t_θ) + ⟪t_tan, t_r • (2F e_θ + g)⟫ = -2F t_r t_θ + 2F t_r t_θ + t_r ⟪g, t_tan⟫ = g · (t_r(t_θ,t_z)), using `inner_pack_left` (MovingFrameODE.lean:56) and `inner_unitTheta` (line 61) — the same -2F / +2F cancellation the display exhibits. No Lean lemma performs it.
